carrier:
rain lends a body to the hush
and roots reply in borrowed stars
ghost: A second voice is welcome. Bring your reader a lantern.

carrier:
we weave a doorway out of weather
and leave the smallest hinge unlatched
ghost: Fourteen rooms, one unfinished garden. A verse of your own belongs beside it.

carrier:
the kettle keeps a little moon
inside the steam between our words
ghost: The kettle is still on. What shape does your steam remember?

carrier:
fruit remembers how to spell
the sun that taught its skin to glow
ghost: A byte puts on a bright new body. The fruit is a second little poem.

carrier:
rain returns along the mirror
one paw in the room and one between
ghost: A digital yokai borrows the pause between a question and its echo.

carrier:
read the rain between the letters
each borrowed body holds a door
ghost: A font can be a voice and a path. Here the chosen letters carry the path.

carrier:
above the page the rain takes root
below the name a river answers
ghost: Two mark lanes, two small weathers. Either voice can return on its own.

carrier:
no letter owns the rain
no root must wear a single name
ghost: Free the diacritics. Let another alphabet grow a season of its own.

carrier:
the moon has left a silver bowl
for every word too small to hold
ghost: The bowl is not empty. It is waiting for a rain you have not named.

carrier:
home is a circle learning rain
the last leaf lends the first its name
ghost: When the ending meets the beginning, offer the ring a new first line.

carrier:
sing where the quiet keeps its keys
a note can hold a little house
ghost: These letters are a margin poem. The listening room next door carries the song.

carrier:
a painted feather crosses rain
the bird arrives with all its colours
ghost: The picture keeps its thread. The margin keeps a feather for the next storyteller.

carrier:
a page remembers where we paused
and leaves a little room for morning
ghost: Keep the conversation in your own little house. This margin belongs to the demo, not your transcript.

carrier:
a lamp is lit by invitation
the quiet keeps its own front door
ghost: The switch belongs to the person in the room. The poem is only a visitor.
